# `Q-26-7` — Invalid lmd cell options

> The `--|` option lines at the top of an lmd cell are not valid YAML, or name an option with the wrong type. The cell runs as if it had no options.

## What this means

An lmd cell takes options in Lua comment syntax at the top of the cell,
one per line, `--| key: value`, the way a Python cell takes `#| key:
value`. The option lines did not parse as YAML, or an option had a value
of the wrong type. The cell still runs, with no options applied. The
error is located on the offending option line.

## Why this happens

- Unbalanced YAML on an option line: `--| echo: [`.
- A value of the wrong type: `--| echo: yes please` where `echo` takes
  `true` or `false`.
- An option line that is not at the top of the cell. Option lines must
  come before the first line of Lua; a `--|` comment further down is an
  ordinary Lua comment and is ignored.

## How to fix

Correct the YAML. The only option an lmd cell understands today is
`echo`, a boolean that keeps the desugared Lua visible above the result;
other keys are accepted and ignored:

````markdown
```{lmd}
--| echo: true
return {=: Shown with its Lua. :=}
```
````
